# Part 1 {.center-slide}

**The Problem With Preferential Data**

## Imagine you're a club president, and you want to figure what drinks to order for the next major event...

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%" .fragment}
You run a quick poll asking every member to **rank their preferred drinks** - most to least preferred.

| Member | 1st | 2nd | 3rd |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|
| Alice  | Coffee | Coke | OJ |
| Ben    | Coke | OJ | Coffee |
| Carla  | OJ | Coffee | Coke |
| ...    | ... | ... | ... |
:::

::: {.column width="50%" .fragment}
After the poll, you summarise **first preferences** across the group:

```{r}
#| echo: false
composition_tbl <- tibble(
  Drink = c("Coke", "Orange Juice", "Coffee"),
  `Share (%)` = c(30, 20, 50)
)
kable(composition_tbl, align = "lr") |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 22)
```
:::

::::

## One group → easy to visualise

Very visible that coffee is the most popular choice. 

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-height: 4

composition_long <- tibble(
  campus = "Your Club",
  Coke = 0.30, `Orange Juice` = 0.20, Coffee = 0.50
) |>
  pivot_longer(-campus, names_to = "drink", values_to = "pct")

ggplot(composition_long, aes(x = campus, y = pct, fill = drink)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, width = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 1)),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Coke" = "#E74C3C",
                               "Orange Juice" = "#F39C12",
                               "Coffee" = "#6F4E37")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

## What if you run the same poll in all 4 Monash campuses?

Visualizing the data is a bit more challenging, but it’s still possible to see the differences between the campuses.

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-height: 4.5

composition_tbl <- tibble(
  campus = c("Clayton", "Caulfield", "Peninsula", "Parkville"),
  Coke = c(0.70, 0.20, 0.10, 0.05),
  `Orange Juice` = c(0.10, 0.60, 0.15, 0.25),
  Coffee = c(0.20, 0.20, 0.75, 0.70)
)

composition_long <- composition_tbl |>
  pivot_longer(-campus, names_to = "drink", values_to = "pct")

ggplot(composition_long, aes(x = campus, y = pct, fill = drink)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 1)),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
            color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 4.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Coke" = "#E74C3C",
                               "Orange Juice" = "#F39C12",
                               "Coffee" = "#6F4E37")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 18) +
  theme(legend.position = "right", panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

## But what if you run this poll across all university campuses in Australia? 😬

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-height: 4.5

set.seed(42)
n_campuses <- 150

composition_tbl <- tibble(
  campus = paste0("Campus_", 1:n_campuses),
  Coke = runif(n_campuses, 0.05, 0.80),
  `Orange Juice` = runif(n_campuses, 0.05, 0.80),
  Coffee = 1 - Coke - `Orange Juice`
) |>
  mutate(across(Coke:`Orange Juice`, ~ pmax(pmin(., 0.90), 0.05))) |>
  mutate(Coffee = 1 - Coke - `Orange Juice`) |>
  filter(Coffee > 0, Coke > 0, `Orange Juice` > 0)

composition_long <- composition_tbl |>
  pivot_longer(-campus, names_to = "drink", values_to = "pct")

ggplot(composition_long, aes(x = campus, y = pct, fill = drink)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Coke" = "#E74C3C",
                               "Orange Juice" = "#F39C12",
                               "Coffee" = "#6F4E37")) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "right",
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, size = 5),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
```

## This is the case of Australian Federal Election

- **150 electorates** across Australia in 2025
- Voters **rank all candidates** (preferential voting)
- There are **more than 3 parties**
- Preferences are redistributed round by round until one candidate has majority
- Result: a **composition** of ALP, LNP, Other support for each electorate - across every round of counting

## Enter: the ternary plot

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/abcnews.png)

::: {.small-text}
*[ABC News](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2025-04-24/election-data-rise-independents-major-party-drift/105144918) published this ternary plot for the 2025 House of Representatives results*
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {.incremental}
- Each **dot** = one electorate
- Three components: **ALP %, LNP %, Other %**
- All 150 electorates visible **at once**
- Position in the triangle encodes composition
:::

:::

::::

# Part 2 {.center-slide}

**How to Read a Ternary Plot**

## Each axis measures one party's share

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

```{r axis-demo}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 5.5

# Build a base ternary with axis labels for teaching
p_base <- ggplot(
  input_p2d_base |> filter(CountNumber == 0),
  aes(x = x1, y = x2)
) +
  add_ternary_base() +
  geom_ternary_region(
    x1 = 1/3, x2 = 1/3, x3 = 1/3,
    aes(fill = after_stat(vertex_labels)),
    vertex_labels = tern_2d$vertex_labels,
    alpha = 0.25, color = NA, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  add_vertex_labels(tern_2d$simplex_vertices) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("ALP" = "#E13940", "LNP" = "#1C4F9C", "Other" = "#95A5A6")
  ) +
  theme_void()

# Find one electorate strongly dominated by each party
strong_alp   <- input_p2d_base |> filter(CountNumber == 0) |> arrange(desc(ALP))   |> slice(1)
strong_lnp   <- input_p2d_base |> filter(CountNumber == 0) |> arrange(desc(LNP))   |> slice(1)
strong_other <- input_p2d_base |> filter(CountNumber == 0) |> arrange(desc(Other)) |> slice(1)

# Centroid of the simplex (exact 1/3, 1/3, 1/3 position)
center_pt <- data.frame(
  x1 = mean(tern_2d$simplex_vertices$x1),
  x2 = mean(tern_2d$simplex_vertices$x2)
)

p_base +
  # Three extreme points
  geom_point(data = strong_alp,   size = 4, color = "#E13940") +
  geom_point(data = strong_lnp,   size = 4, color = "#1C4F9C") +
  geom_point(data = strong_other, size = 4, color = "#10C25B") +
  # Centre point (diamond shape to distinguish)
  geom_point(data = center_pt, size = 5, color = "#8E44AD", shape = 18) +
  # Labels for extreme points
  annotate("text", x = strong_alp$x1,   y = strong_alp$x2 - 0.05,
           label = "Sydney (ALP: 55.1%)",   color = "#E13940", size = 3.2,  fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = strong_lnp$x1,   y = strong_lnp$x2 - 0.05,
           label = "Mananoa (LNP: 53.2%)",   color = "#1C4F9C", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = strong_other$x1, y = strong_other$x2 + 0.05,
           label = "Solomon (Other: 67.2%)", color = "#10C25B", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  # Label for centre
  annotate("text", x = center_pt$x1, y = center_pt$x2 + 0.05,
           label = "Centre (33% each)", color = "#8E44AD", size = 3, fontface = "bold")
```

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {.incremental}
- **Three vertices** — one for each party
- The closer a point is to a vertex, the more support for that party (see Sydney, Mananoa, and Solomon)
- Central point = equal compositions of all parties (33% each)
- The three shares always sum to **100%**
:::

:::

# Part 4 {.center-slide}

**Recreate the example with `prefviz`**

## Function overview

| Step | Function | What it does |
|:----:|:---------|:-------------|
| **1. Data transformation** | `dop_transform()` - for raw ballot data <br/> `dop_irv()` - for aggregated preferences | Reshapes data to compositional format |
| **2. Construct ternary components** | `as_ternable()` - create `ternable` object <br/> `get_tern_*()` - Getter functions for transforming components to appropriate shapes | Builds the simplex object (vertices, edges, coordinates) |
| **3. Visualization** | `ggplot2` & `tourr` extensions | Interactive 2D or high-dimensional plots |

## Step 1: Transform the data

Raw data is from AEC’s 2025 House of Representatives distribution of preferences (same as your assignment!).

```{r}
pref25_2d <- aecdop_2025 |> 
  filter(CalculationType == "Preference Percent") |>
  mutate(Party = case_when(
    !(PartyAb %in% c("LP", "ALP", "NP", "LNP", "LNQ")) ~ "Other", 
    PartyAb %in% c("LP", "NP", "LNP", "LNQ") ~ "LNP",
    TRUE ~ PartyAb
  ))
  
print(
  head(
    pref25_2d |> 
    select(StateAb, DivisionNm, CountNumber, PartyAb, Elected, CalculationValue), 
  5), width = Inf)
```

## Step 1: Transform the data

Transformed data with 3 columns representing the composition of each party in each electorate, summing to 1.

```{r step1}
#| echo: true

pref25_2d <- dop_transform(
  data             = pref25_2d,
  key_cols         = c(DivisionNm, CountNumber),
  value_col        = CalculationValue,
  item_col         = Party,
  winner_col       = Elected,
  winner_identifier = "Y"
)
pref25_2d
```

## Step 2: Get components of ternary plots via `ternable` object

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

A `ternable` object contains the data and metadata necessary for ternary plots, including the **vertices, edges, labels** of the simplex, and **coordinates** of all data points.

```{r step2}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false

tern_2d <- as_ternable(pref25_2d, items = ALP:Other)
```

::: {.incremental}
- **`ternary_coords`** - coordinates of all data points
- **`simplex_vertices`** - coordinates of the 3 corners
- **`simplex_edges`** - pairs connecting vertices
- **`vertex_labels`** - party names at each corner

:::

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

![](images/draw.png)

:::

::::

## Step 3: Visualize (2D) — extract coordinates

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

```{r step3-show-1}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
#| code-line-numbers: "1-2"

input_data <- get_tern_data(tern_2d, plot_type = "2D")

ggplot(input_data |> filter(CountNumber == 0),
       aes(x = x1, y = x2)) +
  add_ternary_base() +
  geom_ternary_region(
    x1 = 1/3, x2 = 1/3, x3 = 1/3,
    aes(fill = after_stat(vertex_labels)),
    vertex_labels = tern_2d$vertex_labels,
    alpha = 0.3, color = NA, show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  add_vertex_labels(tern_2d$simplex_vertices) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Winner)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = party_colors)
```

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

```{r step3-plot-1}
#| echo: false

input_data_v <- get_tern_data(tern_2d, plot_type = "2D")
kable(
  head(input_data_v |> filter(CountNumber == 0) |>
         select(DivisionNm, x1, x2, Winner), 6),
  digits = 3, align = "lccl", col.names = c("Electorate", "x1", "x2", "Winner")
) |>
  kable_styling(font_size = 14)
```

:::

## Step 3: High-dimensional (5 parties)

`prefviz` depends on `tourr` for high-dimensional visualization, and `detourr` for interactive tours.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="60%"}

```{r step3-3}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
#| code-line-numbers: "6-8"
color_vector <- c(rep("black", 5),
  party_colors[pref25_hd$Winner])

# Animate the tour
animate_xy(
  get_tern_data(tern_hd, plot_type = "HD"),  # Get data from ternable
  edges = get_tern_edges(tern_hd), # Get edges from ternable
  obs_labels  = get_tern_labels(tern_hd), # Get labels from ternable
  col = color_vector,
  axes = "bottomleft"
)
```
